Strings on the roof

The engine's strings drawn on the positions they wire: option A by string and by MPPT, option D by inverter with its two inverters; a string traced under the pointer and selected with its callout; the plan; on phone.

S1 · S7 · S13 · S19S2 · S8 · S14 · S20S3 · S9 · S15 · S21S4 · S10 · S16 · S22S5 · S11 · S17S6 · S12 · S18Not used

Option A at 1500 V, the engine's 22 strings of 29 modules, each drawn on the positions it wires (strings, modules by layout idx). String Sk takes series colour ((k − 1) mod 6) + 1: S1, S7, S13 and S19 share the first colour, S6, S12 and S18 the sixth (decision 12).

The engine numbers the strings along the rows, so neighbours in a row never share a colour; across rows one may meet another of its colour. The legend names, for each colour, the strings it marks; the trace and the callout tell two apart (decision 13).

The 152 positions A does not use are moduleUnused, grey. INV-1 is a small box in the accent at the engine's place, (31.04, 39.0), on the north edge inside the setback, with its chip.

By string the legend takes a second line under the switch: the six colours do not fit beside it. The light and the shadows are of 10:30 on 21 December, the time the stage opens at; the time pill and the vitals are left out of these crops.

Coloured by MPPT

Desktop stage, option A by MPPT
INV-1

22 strings of 29 modules · 1 inverter, 6 MPPT · 152 positions not used
MPPT 1MPPT 2MPPT 3MPPT 4MPPT 5MPPT 6Not used

The same strings coloured by the MPPT each is wired to (mppt): MPPT 1 the first series colour, MPPT 6 the sixth, as on the approved board, where the stage opens. The legend is the approved one.

The engine fills the MPPTs in the order of the strings: MPPT 1 takes 4, MPPT 2 takes 4, MPPT 3 takes 4, MPPT 4 takes 4, MPPT 5 takes 3, MPPT 6 takes 3 strings; so the colours follow the rows of the roof, the lowest rows MPPT 1.

A string of another inverter's MPPT 3 takes the colour of MPPT 3 too: by MPPT is the MPPT within its inverter.

Option D, 26 × 27 on two inverters, coloured by inverter: INV-1 the first series colour, INV-2 the second. Its 27 strings use 702 positions; 88 are not used.

Both markers stand where the engine places them: INV-1 at (27.37, 1.0) on the south edge, near the strings it takes, INV-2 at (36.92, 39.0) on the north edge. Each is a small box in inverterMarker with its chip, placed by the Projector.

D is below the DC/AC target; it is shown here for its two inverters. The line under the title counts them: 2 inverters, 6 MPPT each.

A string traced and selected

Traced under the pointer: string 12 of option A, coloured by MPPT
INV-1
Pressed: string 12 selected, with its callout
INV-1
String 12 · INV-1, MPPT 3
29 modules · Voc cold 1,480 V · 93 m of cable

Under the pointer a string is traced (decision 13): its glass stringSelected, white; every other position its colour mixed 55 % toward the stage; a line of 2 in white through the middles of its modules in the order they are wired (modules of S12, 29 of them: east along the northern line of the row, then back west along the southern). The stair room's kept-clear area splits it in two runs. On touch there is no trace.

A press selects it and the callout says the string, its inverter and its MPPT, its modules, its Voc cold and its metres of cable, from the engine's cable schedule of A: 1,480 V and 93.2 m, shown as 93 m. The swatch is the string's colour of the moment, here MPPT 3's. The callout's line and dot are in the accent, as every callout on the stage; the string's white is for its glass and its trace line only. The chip stands over the dot on a line of 40.

The approved board said 63 m of cable for string 12; the engine's schedule says 93.2 m, and the board follows the engine.

On phone a tap selects a string; nothing is traced. The callout, its line and dot in the accent, hangs under the dot, since the time and the view controls fill the top of the stage, and wraps in a chip of 264. The colour switch and the legend are in the sheet (the lens's phone board).
